content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Circulating Cholesterol Fuels SARS-CoV-2 Replication Through Viral ORF3a Receptor Stabilization by November 14, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Circulating Cholesterol Fuels SARS-CoV-2 Replication Through Viral ORF3a Receptor Stabilization Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram SARS-CoV-2 exploits extracellular low-density lipoprotein to accelerate viral ribonucleic acid replication within infected host tissues, operating through the viral accessory protein ORF3a. In cell culture systems, human airway organoid models, and small animal infection studies, researchers established that circulating cholesterol directly stimulates viral genome synthesis rather than viral attachment, entry, or structural assembly. The investigation demonstrated that elevated levels of low-density lipoprotein, commonly referred to as bad cholesterol, provide essential lipids that the pathogen repurposes to construct specialized intracellular replication organelles. While previous epidemiological observations noted that individuals with pre-existing metabolic conditions suffered significantly worse disease trajectories, the molecular mechanisms connecting circulating lipoproteins to viral replication efficiency had remained largely unexplained. By tracing the cellular uptake of labeled cholesterol particles and tracking viral double-stranded ribonucleic acid accumulation, the investigators showed that extracellular cholesterol availability directly dictates the speed and magnitude of coronaviral genomic replication across human airway cells. Metabolic comorbidities such as advanced age, obesity, and type 2 diabetes have consistently correlated with severe COVID-19 manifestations and increased patient mortality throughout the global pandemic. Prior clinical reports documented that patients receiving statin therapy to lower circulating low-density lipoprotein exhibited milder disease progressions, whereas individuals possessing the apolipoprotein E4 genetic variant, which elevates circulating low-density lipoprotein concentrations, suffered heightened morbidity. Additionally, clinical evaluations of fenofibrate, a therapeutic agent that stimulates lipoprotein lipase activity, reported reduced intracellular lipid accumulation and improved survival among infected individuals. Animal experiments utilizing diet-induced obesity in rodents similarly corroborated the pathological contribution of circulating lipids to coronavirus pathogenesis. However, whether extracellular lipoproteins actively participated in biochemical events within infected cells remained an unresolved question. Because respiratory tissues rely on circulating lipoprotein complexes to supply approximately eighty percent of their cellular cholesterol requirements, researchers hypothesized that host cholesterol scavenging pathways might directly nourish the replicative cycle of SARS-CoV-2. To evaluate how specific extracellular lipids influence infection dynamics, the research team exposed cultured human lung cells and organoids to purified lipid fractions prior to viral inoculation. Experiments utilizing A549 lung carcinoma cells overexpressing the human ACE2 receptor and primary human airway organoids revealed that low-density lipoprotein supplementation significantly elevated viral ribonucleic acid synthesis. Quantifying viral nucleocapsid and envelope genes via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction confirmed elevated intracellular viral transcripts. Furthermore, low-density lipoprotein and very low-density lipoprotein treatments expanded the proportion of infected cells displaying double-stranded viral ribonucleic acid, whereas high-density lipoprotein or oleic acid supplementation produced no measurable enhancement. Because oleic acid stimulated triglyceride synthesis without driving infection, and high-density lipoprotein operates primarily in cholesterol efflux rather than massive import, the authors deduced that targeted cholesterol internalization was specifically required. Pharmacological inhibition of PCSK9 using the small molecule (R)-IMPP increased low-density lipoprotein receptor abundance, which subsequently amplified viral infection rates in treated cellular cultures. Discover more Cholesterol cholesterol Lower Cholesterol Meet Dietitians Get Rapid Tests To pinpoint the exact phase of the viral lifecycle supported by cholesterol, the scientists deployed several specialized subgenomic model systems. First, pseudotyped lentiviral particles displaying the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein and carrying luciferase reporter genes were used to isolate viral entry mechanisms. Adding low-density lipoprotein failed to alter luciferase signal in target cells expressing ACE2 alone or cells co-expressing ACE2 and the transmembrane serine protease TMPRSS2, indicating that cholesterol does not directly facilitate receptor-mediated viral entry. Next, virus-like particles containing all viral structural proteins were utilized to assess viral assembly and egress; low-density lipoprotein treatment again produced no measurable change in particle generation or luciferase transfer. In sharp contrast, single-round replicon systems lacking the envelope gene and harboring a secreted nanoluciferase reporter demonstrated substantial luminescence increases following low-density lipoprotein administration. These replicon findings established that the primary benefit of extracellular cholesterol occurs downstream of entry during intracellular genomic replication. Microscopic examinations confirmed that extracellular cholesterol actively fuels the physical assembly of intracellular replication complexes. Staining experiments demonstrated that replicon-bearing cells treated with low-density lipoprotein developed significantly larger double-stranded ribonucleic acid foci and higher overall viral transcript levels. When investigators exposed lung cells to infectious virus for one hour, washed away unattached virions, and then introduced low-density lipoprotein, viral replication surged three-fold for the ancestral WA1 strain and four-fold for the Beta variant over seventy-two hours. Correlative light and electron microscopy of infected Vero cells further illuminated dramatic ultrastructural reorganizations occurring within host cytoplasm. Cells cultured in the presence of low-density lipoprotein displayed an elevated abundance and packing density of double-membrane vesicles, which serve as protective membrane hubs for viral replication, alongside numerous open double-membrane spherules. To identify which viral component orchestrates this lipid scavenging program, the researchers systematically screened individual viral proteins expressed within human lung cells. Using fluorescent DiI-labeled low-density lipoprotein to quantify particle uptake, they found that authentic viral infection increased cellular low-density lipoprotein uptake by approximately twenty percent. Strikingly, expressing the accessory protein ORF3a alone increased particle internalization by more than thirty percent relative to empty vector controls. Other viral proteins, including non-structural proteins NSP1, NSP2, NSP6, and NSP12, significantly suppressed lipoprotein uptake, highlighting that ORF3a exerts a dominant activating role during authentic infection. Lipid profiling via thin-layer chromatography corroborated that infected cells accumulated substantial stores of cholesterol esters, the principal intracellular storage format for imported cholesterol. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction further verified that infection upregulated critical host uptake factors, including the low-density lipoprotein receptor and NPC1, illustrating that the virus systematically drives cellular machinery to replenish intracellular cholesterol reserves. Mechanistic investigations revealed that ORF3a directly interacts with and stabilizes the host low-density lipoprotein receptor within intracellular endosomes. Confocal microscopy demonstrated that FLAG-tagged ORF3a co-localized extensively with green fluorescent protein-tagged low-density lipoprotein receptors in cultured cells, while co-immunoprecipitation confirmed their physical association. Notably, ORF3a expression led to the preferential enrichment of higher molecular weight bands representing mature receptors rather than newly synthesized precursors located in the endoplasmic reticulum. By binding to mature receptors within endosomes, ORF3a hindered the association between the receptor and PCSK9, a regulatory chaperone that normally triggers receptor breakdown within lysosomes. Cycloheximide chase experiments confirmed that ORF3a expression prolonged receptor half-life in host cells. Flow cytometry showed that surface receptor presentation and recycling via CCC and WASH protein complexes remained intact. CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts targeting the low-density lipoprotein receptor, NPC1, or NPC2 severely impaired viral infection, proving that intact host cholesterol uptake machinery is vital for the viral cycle. To validate whether ORF3a drives cholesterol-dependent pathogenesis in living organisms, the researchers conducted in vivo infection experiments using Golden Syrian hamsters. Male hamsters were preconditioned for two weeks on either a standard laboratory rodent chow or a high-cholesterol diet formulated with fifteen percent lard and zero-point-five percent cholesterol. Animals were then intranasally inoculated with ancestral WA1 virus or an engineered mutant possessing a premature stop codon at the initial amino acid position of ORF3a, designated ORF3a-STOP. In hamsters infected with the ancestral strain, consuming a high-cholesterol diet produced a statistically significant increase in infectious virion titers and elevated nucleocapsid antigen staining across lung tissues. In marked contrast, hamsters infected with the ORF3a-STOP mutant displayed no increase in viral titers or lung tissue pathology when fed the high-cholesterol diet. The investigation further unraveled an evolutionary divergence between viral lineages, explaining why the Beta variant responded with the strongest replication enhancement upon low-density lipoprotein exposure. The Beta genome carries two specific point mutations in ORF3a: Q57H and S171L. While ancestral ORF3a binds host VPS39, a component of the HOPS tethering complex, affinity purification mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated that the S171L mutation markedly abrogates this interaction. Ancestral ORF3a deacidifies endosomes through its VPS39 interaction, inadvertently impairing acid-dependent cholesterol ester hydrolysis from internalized particles. Conversely, Beta ORF3a maintains endosomal acidification, as demonstrated by elevated fluorescence in LDL-pHrodo Red live imaging assays. By preserving luminal acidification while continuing to stabilize the low-density lipoprotein receptor, Beta ORF3a optimizes both particle endocytosis and subsequent enzymatic cholesterol liberation. Stable expression of Beta ORF3a or the single S171L mutant in Calu-3 cells rescued replication of the ORF3a-STOP virus to a substantially greater extent than ancestral ORF3a. In contrast to the Beta lineage, the Omicron variant exhibited diminished sensitivity to extracellular low-density lipoprotein, aligning with its altered clinical profile. Genomic sequencing shows that Omicron BA.1 carries ancestral-like ORF3a sequences lacking the Beta mutations, while earlier studies documented that Omicron expresses lower overall levels of ORF3a messenger RNA and protein. Although these findings explain why hypercholesterolemic hosts faced heightened disease severity during ancestral and Beta variant waves, several mechanistic questions remain open. The authors emphasized that several viral proteins, including NSP3, NSP9, NSP11, NSP16, and ORF7a, have not yet been evaluated for their individual effects on host lipid uptake. Furthermore, while the study establishes a direct biochemical link between circulating cholesterol, receptor stabilization, and double-membrane vesicle formation, translating these cell and animal findings into human antiviral therapies requires targeted clinical investigation before specific cholesterol-modulating protocols can be validated. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health COVID-19 Antibodies Did Not Affect Denosumab Biosimilar Immunogenicity in Clinical Trial by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 COVID-19 Antibodies Did Not Affect Denosumab Biosimilar Immunogenicity in Clinical Trial Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram During the COVID-19 pandemic, drug developers and regulatory authorities faced widespread uncertainty regarding whether adaptive immune responses provoked by natural severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection or newly introduced vaccines might interfere with clinical trial endpoints, particularly the immunogenicity profiles of therapeutic biologics. In an exploratory evaluation conducted within a clinical trial supporting the approval of GP2411—a biosimilar candidate to reference denosumab—investigators implemented a dedicated serology testing framework to monitor anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunoglobulin G (IgG) responses among healthy volunteers. The research demonstrated that the development of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies, whether acquired through natural viral exposure or vaccination, exerted no clinically meaningful impact on the incidence, persistence, or magnitude of anti-drug antibodies directed against the denosumab biosimilar. The underlying clinical trial was conducted in Germany between 2020 and 2022 and enrolled healthy male participants aged 28 to 65 years who received a single dose of denosumab administered as GP2411 or reference Xgeva. Denosumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody engineered to bind receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand (RANKL), thereby preventing activation of its receptor RANK on the surface of osteoclasts and suppressing osteoclastic bone resorption. Because therapeutic proteins carry an inherent potential to stimulate an unwanted immune response in recipients, assessing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) served as a primary secondary endpoint in the trial. To resolve potential confounding factors arising from widespread pandemic exposure, the research team instituted an exploratory serological testing program to evaluate whether immune activation against SARS-CoV-2 could heighten immunogenic sensitivity or cross-react with the biotherapeutic. To evaluate participant serology systematically, the researchers selected and partially validated a commercially available qualitative enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test kit, the SCoV-2 Detect SARS-CoV-2 IgG ELISA developed by InBios International, which held Emergency Use Authorization from the US Food and Drug Administration. This indirect ELISA incorporates the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein as an immobilized capture antigen to detect human IgG antibodies targeting viral epitopes. Initial pre-validation experiments conducted in-house verified the assay’s operational characteristics across a panel of diverse human serum specimens. The kit correctly identified all negative control sera obtained from healthy donors prior to the 2019 outbreak, achieving a confirmed baseline specificity of 100 percent across six unexposed samples, including hemolytic and lipemic controls. Discover more Track Biotech Save on Rx Study Biology Find Treatments In sensitivity testing across different cohorts, the assay detected anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG in 92 percent of hospitalized symptomatic donors evaluated at least 14 days after confirmation by polymerase chain reaction. These hospitalized patients exhibited robust antibody reactivity, yielding immunological status ratio (ISR) values that ranged predominantly between 12.3 and 16.6. When applied to vaccinated individuals, the assay demonstrated 100 percent sensitivity across six serum samples, displaying ISR values between 1.8 and 8.4. Conversely, in non-hospitalized donors with confirmed asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections, the assay identified anti-spike IgG in 57 percent of individuals; retrospective records confirmed that the three non-reactive donors were negative for IgG while testing positive for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgM responses, reflecting earlier-stage humoral adaptation. A pivotal bioanalytical innovation within the study was the formal validation of singlicate sample analysis alongside traditional duplicate testing. Historically, ligand binding assays have relied on duplicate measurements to compensate for potential analytical variance, yet processing clinical samples as singlicates presents opportunities to conserve biological matrix and accelerate high-throughput screening while maintaining compliance with bioanalytical standards. Using freshly prepared validation samples diluted from a verified SARS-CoV-2-positive human serum pool into unexposed healthy volunteer serum, the investigators assessed assay selectivity, precision, and tolerance. Under predefined acceptance criteria requiring a coefficient of variation of 20 percent or lower, singlicate analysis achieved intra-assay precision values ranging from 5 to 11 percent, compared to 3 to 4 percent for duplicates, while inter-assay precision ranged from 8 to 16 percent for singlicates and 8 to 14 percent for duplicates. Discover more Find Vaccines Donate to Research Read Med Journals The validation protocol also examined whether the presence of circulating denosumab or anti-drug antibodies could interfere with the qualitative detection of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies, causing false-positive or false-negative readings. The assay established identical drug tolerance and ADA tolerance thresholds under both singlicate and duplicate evaluation formats, verifying that therapeutic drug concentrations and host antibodies against the monoclonal therapy did not impede accurate serological assessment. To safeguard against borderline ambiguity in routine singlicate execution, a re-analysis algorithm was implemented: any singlicate specimen producing an ISR value between 0.9 and 1.1 was automatically re-tested in duplicate to establish a definitive result. In the subsequent analysis of 1970 clinical study samples, only 24 samples (approximately 1 percent) fell within this equivocal re-analysis window. Serological monitoring across the trial cohort tracked 499 healthy male volunteers over four sequential sampling visits spanning baseline, day 85, day 169, and the formal conclusion of the study. Overall, anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies were detected in 1165 serum samples, establishing an overall study seroprevalence of 82 percent among the trial population. The assay identified viral antibodies in all 55 participants who reported a confirmed COVID-19 infection during the trial. Furthermore, among 325 participants who received an authorized COVID-19 vaccine at least 14 days before sampling, 321 individuals (99 percent) exhibited detectable anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG responses in at least one post-vaccination specimen, aligning with established rates of vaccine seroconversion. At the individual specimen level, 863 serum samples were obtained from participants who either had a verified COVID-19 infection, had completed vaccination at least two weeks prior, or experienced both events. The validated ELISA detected anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG in 835 of these 863 samples, achieving a clinical detection rate of 97 percent. Among the 28 samples lacking detectable IgG, most had been collected shortly after the initial vaccine dose. For the 835 reactive samples, ISR measurements ranged from 1.1 to 7.4, demonstrating comparable overall antibody levels between vaccinated individuals and those with confirmed clinical infection; median ISR values were recorded at 5.8 for vaccinated participants and 6.3 for those with confirmed natural infection. Concurrently, the trial rigorously evaluated the secondary immunogenicity endpoint of the denosumab biosimilar using a drug-tolerant electrochemiluminescence bridging assay sensitive down to 6 nanograms per milliliter in neat serum. Across 6408 clinical serum samples drawn from the 499 dosed participants, 319 individuals (64 percent) tested positive for anti-drug antibodies at some point during follow-up. Crucially, all confirmed ADA-positive samples exhibited very low antibody concentrations, remaining below the formal titer reporting threshold of 20 nanograms per milliliter. Furthermore, anti-drug antibody reactivity proved transient across virtually all participants, with persistent ADAs observed in only three subjects whose seroconversion timing showed no consistent relationship with viral antibody exposure. Neutralizing anti-drug antibodies capable of inhibiting the therapeutic activity of denosumab were extraordinarily rare throughout the trial, appearing in only four serum samples collected from three participants. When cross-referenced against concurrent COVID-19 serology results, neutralizing anti-drug antibody findings displayed no link to SARS-CoV-2 immunity: two neutralizing samples coincided with negative anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG readings, while one matched a positive viral serology result. These findings collectively demonstrated that systemic immune activation provoked by COVID-19 infection or spike-directed vaccination did not augment anti-denosumab antibody titers, alter ADA persistence, or elevate the incidence of neutralizing antibodies, validating the biosimilar’s predictable immunogenicity profile during global pandemic conditions. The study authors highlighted several methodological boundaries, noting that because the authorized ELISA relied exclusively on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, the assay could not distinguish between vaccination-induced antibodies and responses elicited by natural viral infection. In addition, acute infections during the trial were captured via self-reported outside diagnostic testing rather than scheduled in-trial diagnostic swabs, precluding a formal calculation of in-study diagnostic specificity. Nevertheless, the successful deployment of singlicate bioanalytical screening proved robust, demonstrating that efficient, low-volume serology strategies can effectively isolate confounding pandemic variables and support regulatory compliance in clinical trials of biotherapeutic candidates. content: web statistics Sections Malaysia Business World Opinion Sports & Fitness Culture & Lifestyle Podcast Education Videos Gallery About The Team Contact Us Advertising Privacy Policy Terms of Use About Us Get the app Follow us on Health WHO urges testing as new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 mimics flu, common cold symptoms Emerging variant detected across several continents, with reports of severe sore throat and prolonged fatigue raising health concerns Updated 5 days ago · Published on 10 Nov 2026 2:43PM Shares The warning comes as the SARS-CoV-2 lineage, first identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026, has been detected across parts of Asia - November 10, 2026 THE World Health Organisation (WHO) has urged continued diagnostic testing as a newly emerging COVID-19 variant, PJ.2.1, spreads internationally with symptoms that can be mistaken for influenza or the common cold. The warning comes as the SARS-CoV-2 lineage, first identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026, has been detected across North America, Europe, Australia, New Zealand and parts of Asia. WHO said symptoms alone were insufficient to reliably distinguish PJ.2.1 infections from other respiratory illnesses, stressing that diagnostic testing remained the most accurate way to identify the virus. This is particularly important when confirmation of an infection could affect treatment decisions or public health measures. The organisation said it was closely monitoring the variant amid concerns over its growing geographical spread. Preliminary research published in the Journal of Infection suggests PJ.2.1 may have a growth advantage through increased binding to the ACE2 receptor, which enables the coronavirus to enter human cells, rather than through a substantial ability to evade vaccine-induced antibodies. The variant carries multiple mutations in its spike protein, the structure responsible for facilitating infection. Meanwhile, Russian infectious disease specialist and virologist Elena Malinnikova said infections involving PJ.2.1 could cause severe sore throat and prolonged fatigue during recovery compared with some other variants. However, further research is needed to establish whether the variant causes more severe disease, spreads more easily or significantly reduces protection from existing immunity. - November 10, 2026 Popular Trending Spotlight Malaysia Loke urges PM to focus on reforms, not early election pressure Malaysia Melaka declares special holiday tomorrow, in recognition of the people's mandate Malaysia Ab Rauf retains Melaka leadership Malaysia Mahathir makes first major party appearance since Hasmah's death at Pejuang AGM Malaysia Perak Sultan warns against shielding rulers from people's grievances Malaysia Retiree loses RM80k after WhatsApp investment scam demands RM50k to release profits Health Selangor health clinics prioritise emergency cases regardless of patients’ nationality Malaysia Some 243,501 undocumented migrants sent home under Malaysia's repatriation programme Malaysia Police hunt 38-year-old man over fatal stabbing in Kota Kinabalu You may be interested Health Selangor health clinics prioritise emergency cases regardless of patients’ nationality Off beat Penang moves to strengthen position as green manufacturing hub By Ian McIntyre Events Annie Tan looks to keep traditional Asian flavours relevant through modern dining By Alfian Z.M. content: Logo Go Ad-Free Home India World Politics Sports Business Quick Take Columns Entertainment Art & Culture Lifestyle Books Technology Open Avenues Archives Movies Cover Stories Features Health Digital Stories Logo Home India World Politics Entertainment Sports Search NewsWrap HomeLifestyleNew COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 spreads across countries: Symptoms, risks and what the research says New COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 spreads across countries: Symptoms, risks and what the research says Open Bureau Last Updated:November 10, 2026, 17:09 IST Summarise Share Share ADVERTISEMENT First detected in Canada in May 2026, the COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 has since been identified in North America, Europe and parts of Asia. Early laboratory research suggests it may enter human cells more efficiently, but there is currently no evidence that it causes more severe illness or significantly escapes vaccine-induced immunity. Covid-19 Virus FAQsSummarise COVID-19 may no longer dominate daily headlines, but the virus has not stopped evolving. A newly identified lineage, PJ.2.1, is attracting attention after appearing in several countries and displaying genetic changes that researchers are examining closely. Does this mean another major wave is approaching? Are existing vaccines still useful? And should people in India be concerned? COVID-19 testing kits Here is what current research and public health surveillance tell us about the variant. ADVERTISEMENT Sign up for Open Magazine's ad-free experience Enjoy uninterrupted access to premium content and insights. Go Ad-Free What is the new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1? PJ.2.1 is a lineage of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. Researchers describe it as a saltation variant, meaning it emerged with a relatively large number of genetic changes rather than accumulating mutations gradually. COVID-19 testing kits A study published in the Journal of Infection on October 24, 2026, by researchers including Markus Hoffmann and colleagues, traced its origins to MC.10.1.7, a descendant of the JN.1 lineage. Its first documented sample was collected in Ontario, Canada, on May 2, 2026. Open Magazine Latest Edition is Out Now! The Wealth Issue 2026 06 Nov 2026 - Vol 05 | Issue 45 Portraits of Dreamers and Doers under 35 Read Now Where has PJ.2.1 been detected? Is it spreading globally? After its initial detection in Canada, PJ.2.1 was identified in several US states and countries including Spain, France, Israel, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand. Public Health Ontario's genomic surveillance data showed that PJ.2.1 accounted for 25.2% of sequenced SARS-CoV-2 samples between September 20 and October 17, up from 16.9% in the preceding four-week period. Get Rapid Tests Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection also reported PJ.2.1 within its JN.1 lineage surveillance data in its November 5 update. However, that figure represents the broader JN.1 group, not PJ.2.1 alone. Recommended Stories Quick Take | What Is Brain Stacking? Seven Things to Know About the Trend That Wants You Off Your Phone The Music between Us: Poetry, memory and kinship that endure beyond borders The Double Danger The Last Word on Salon: Why Literary Media Is Worth Saving The Diabetes Epidemic Hiding Inside India’s ‘Healthy’ Bodies Why is the PJ.2.1 variant attracting scientific attention? The key question is how effectively the variant can enter human cells. SARS-CoV-2 uses its spike protein to attach to a receptor called ACE2, which is present on human cells. The Journal of Infection study found that PJ.2.1 appeared to bind more efficiently to ACE2 in laboratory experiments. This characteristic could help explain its growth, although laboratory findings alone cannot establish how easily it spreads between people. Infection control products Researchers also examined its ability to evade antibodies. They found no substantial additional immune escape compared with most of the other variants tested. ADVERTISEMENT What are the symptoms of the PJ.2.1 COVID-19 variant? There is currently no confirmed symptom pattern unique to PJ.2.1. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), common COVID-19 symptoms include: Fever and chills, sore throat, persistent cough, runny or blocked nose, headache and body aches, fatigue and weakness, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea. Some people may also experience changes in their sense of taste or smell. The WHO cautions that COVID-19 symptoms can overlap with those of influenza and other respiratory infections. Symptoms alone cannot reliably establish which virus has caused an illness; testing may be necessary. More from the author Open Bureau Quick Take | What Is Brain Stacking? Seven Things to Know About the Trend That Wants You Off Your Phone India Beat New Zealand by 22 Runs to Seal ODI Series as Pacers Lead the Way Kate Middleton Joins Prince William in Mumbai for Their First Overseas Tour Together Since 2022 ‘Because of Your Dk?’ Australian PM caught in embarrassing hot mic gaffe With Chris Bowen Is PJ.2.1 more dangerous than previous COVID-19 variants? There is not enough clinical evidence to conclude that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease, hospitalisations or deaths. The research published in the Journal of Infection primarily examined the variant's genetic characteristics, cell entry and antibody sensitivity. It did not establish that people infected with PJ.2.1 are more likely to develop serious complications. Older adults, people with weakened immune systems and those with underlying conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and chronic respiratory illnesses remain at greater risk of severe COVID-19. ADVERTISEMENT Do existing COVID-19 vaccines protect against PJ.2.1? The laboratory findings offer some reassurance. Researchers found that antibodies from people who had received an LP.8.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccine could neutralise PJ.2.1. Its sensitivity to neutralisation was 1.8 times lower than that of the LP.8.1 reference variant. This suggests that the variant has not demonstrated a dramatic ability to escape vaccine-induced antibodies. However, laboratory neutralisation results do not establish how well a vaccine prevents infection in everyday conditions. The WHO continues to recommend COVID-19 vaccination for people at highest risk of severe disease, including older adults and individuals with certain underlying conditions. Has PJ.2.1 been detected in India? Should people be worried? There is currently no verified public confirmation that PJ.2.1 has been detected in India. The Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium (INSACOG) monitors changes in circulating coronavirus strains through a network of sequencing laboratories, but its publicly available dashboard does not identify PJ.2.1 as a confirmed Indian detection. There is also an important distinction in the WHO's classification. Its latest published variant-tracking information lists JN.1 as a variant of interest and XFG, NB.1.8.1, PQ.16.1.1 and BA.3.2 as variants under monitoring. PJ.2.1 is not separately listed in those categories. For now, the emergence of PJ.2.1 calls for continued surveillance rather than alarm. Maintaining vaccination among vulnerable groups, practising good respiratory hygiene and seeking medical advice when symptoms become concerning remain sensible precautions. The research is still developing, and whether this lineage will have a significant impact on global COVID-19 trends remains to be seen. (With inputs from ANI) Frequently Asked Questions What is the new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1? - PJ.2.1 is a SARS-CoV-2 lineage described as a saltation variant, emerging with many genetic changes. Its first sample was collected in Ontario, Canada, on May 2, 2026. Where has the PJ.2.1 variant been detected globally? + PJ.2.1 was detected in Canada, several US states, Spain, France, Israel, Singapore, Australia, and New Zealand. Public Health Ontario reported it accounted for 25.2% of sequenced samples by October 17. Why is the PJ.2.1 variant attracting scientific attention? + Scientists are examining PJ.2.1 because laboratory experiments suggest it binds more efficiently to the ACE2 receptor on human cells, potentially explaining its growth. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health AZD7442 Antibody and Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccine Are Well Tolerated in Immunocompromised Adults by November 13, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 AZD7442 Antibody and Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccine Are Well Tolerated in Immunocompromised Adults Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 followed by a bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine was well tolerated with no serious adverse events in immunocompromised adults, according to findings from the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled RAPID-PROTECTION trial. The clinical trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of the combination regimen in 139 immunocompromised adult participants who remain highly vulnerable to severe COVID-19 infection. Under the study protocol, participants received the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 followed 28 days later by the bivalent vaccine. Pharmacokinetic monitoring showed that serum concentrations of AZD7442 peaked at day 28 following administration. Circulating concentrations of the monoclonal antibody remained detectable across different disease cohorts through day 180 of follow-up. Discover more Study Biology vaccines Vaccine vaccine Find Vaccines Humoral immune evaluations revealed that anti-Spike antibody responses increased following AZD7442 administration and reached their highest measured levels after subsequent vaccination. However, while binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, functional neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Detailed epitope mapping showed that vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies directed against the S2 subunit, the S1 N-terminal domain, and receptor-binding domain epitopes distinct from those bound by AZD7442. Vaccination was also observed to increase S2-specific memory B cells among participants. In addition to humoral responses, vaccine-induced T-cell responses demonstrated cross-reactivity between ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron variants. The trial investigators concluded that these findings support the consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development, with the study registered under ISRCTN53507177. The multicentre RAPID-PROTECTION clinical trial evaluated this intervention using an open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial design focused on immunocompromised adults who remain at high risk of severe COVID-19. Study participants received the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and were subsequently administered the bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine twenty-eight days later. Across the cohort of 139 adult patients, clinical monitoring confirmed that the long-acting monoclonal antibody was well tolerated, with investigators documenting no serious adverse events throughout the trial protocol. The study was officially registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry under identifier ISRCTN53507177. Discover more COVID-19 vaccine Get Rapid Tests COVID-19 Vaccine COVID-19 vaccination Read Health News Pharmacokinetic assessments tracked circulating drug levels over extended observation periods to determine antibody persistence in this highly vulnerable population. Serum concentrations of AZD7442 reached their peak at day 28 following administration, coinciding with the timing of subsequent vaccination. Longitudinal follow-up further established that serum AZD7442 remained detectable across different disease cohorts through day 180. Alongside these pharmacokinetic measurements, assessments of humoral immunogenicity demonstrated that anti-Spike antibody responses rose following the initial AZD7442 administration and reached their highest measured levels after participants received the bivalent mRNA/LNP vaccination. Detailed analysis of antibody targets revealed distinct patterns of humoral immune activation following the sequential regimen. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting the S2 subunit, the S1 N-terminal domain, and receptor-binding domain epitopes that were not bound by AZD7442 itself. In addition to expanding circulating antibody breadth, the bivalent vaccination increased the presence of S2-specific memory B cells in the immunosuppressed participants. However, the trial identified notable boundaries in humoral protection against circulating viral variants. Although binding antibodies directed against Omicron variants increased after vaccination, functional neutralisation of Omicron remained limited following both the initial AZD7442 administration and the subsequent vaccine dose. While neutralising antibody activity against Omicron was constrained, evaluations of cellular immunity showed broader activity across SARS-CoV-2 strains. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses proved cross-reactive between ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron variants, demonstrating that cellular responses remained capable of recognising divergent viral lineages. Because immunocompromised individuals continue to face serious risks from SARS-CoV-2 infection, these combined immunological and pharmacokinetic findings provide direct empirical support for future therapeutic development. The investigators concluded that the documented safety, cellular cross-reactivity, and pharmacokinetic stability support the consideration of combined monoclonal antibody and vaccination strategies in future therapeutic antibody development programs. content_title: Could a common diabetes drug help prevent long COVID?
content: A nationwide study suggests that prescribing the widely used diabetes drug metformin soon after COVID-19 infection may substantially reduce the risk of long COVID or death, reinforcing earlier clinical trial findings. Study: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Image credit: TBamphoto/Shutterstock.com Prescription of metformin within six days of documented severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 ( SARS-CoV-2 ) infection is associated with a 53% lower risk of developing long COVID or death over six months, according to a new study published in the Journal of Medical Virology . Metformin emerges as a potential long COVID preventive SARS-CoV-2, the causative pathogen of the coronavirus disease 2019 ( COVID-19 ) pandemic, continues to cause new infections across countries. Long COVID refers to symptoms that persist or develop following SARS-CoV-2 infection, typically lasting at least three months, and has become a major public health concern worldwide. Long COVID is also associated with a significant economic burden, highlighting the need for identifying medications that can reduce the risk of developing long COVID. Metformin, a widely used medication for type 2 diabetes, has shown the ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 in in vitro studies. In a randomized clinical trial, patients receiving metformin were found to have lower nasal viral load and a reduced risk of developing long COVID. However, the trial restricted enrollment by age and body mass index, and only 22% were enrolled during the Omicron era. These factors might have restricted the generalizability of its findings to patients with diverse sociodemographic and health conditions. The current study aimed to investigate the association between newly prescribed metformin at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of developing long COVID in a broader sample, using electronic health records. Nationwide health records help assess metformin and long COVID The study analyzed electronic health record data from a nationwide database containing over 21 million individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection from every state in the United States to identify new metformin users who were prescribed the drug within six days of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. New metformin users were compared with those prescribed comparator medications, including fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast, for the risk of long COVID or death within 180 days of the metformin or comparator medication prescription. The researchers excluded patients with documented indications for chronic metformin use, including diabetes and prediabetes, as well as those prescribed metformin or comparator medications in the preceding 12 months. Eligible patients were also required to have attended outpatient visits during both the 0–6-month and 6–12-month periods before infection. Early metformin prescriptions linked to lower long COVID risk The study included 248 patients in the metformin group and a comparator group with a weighted size equivalent to approximately 248 patients. In most cases, medications were prescribed within two days of SARS-CoV-2 infection, suggesting successful identification of patients who were seeking metformin or control medications for their infection. The analysis of primary outcomes showed that, after weighting, about 4% of patients in the metformin group and 8.5% of patients in the control group had long COVID or died, representing an absolute difference of approximately 4.5 percentage points. Download the latest edition The adjusted risk ratio analysis indicated that patients who received a metformin prescription within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection had a 53% lower risk of long COVID or death over a 6-month period, compared with those who received a prescription for comparator medications. Further analysis suggested that having a metformin prescription within one day of infection was associated with a 61% lower risk of long COVID or death, whereas having the same prescription within 14 days of infection was associated with a 25% lower risk. Real-world findings reinforce earlier metformin clinical trial results The study provides further evidence of an association between newly prescribed metformin during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and a lower risk of long COVID or death over a period of six months. The association appeared stronger in patients who received metformin earlier in infection. These findings are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that early initiation of antiviral treatment against SARS-CoV-2 infection is more effective in reducing viral replication than late-stage treatment. Previous in vitro studies have also indicated that metformin reduces SARS-CoV-2 RNA while increasing cell viability. Similarly, previous randomized clinical trials have shown reduced viral load in patients using metformin. In the subgroup excluding those with a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription, the study found a slightly higher risk ratio. This finding raises the hypothesis that patients receiving a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription in addition to a new metformin prescription may have a lower risk ratio than the entire study population. Because of the observational design, the study analyses may be limited by missing data and misclassification of exposures, outcomes, and confounders. Since nirmatrelvir–ritonavir could be obtained directly from pharmacies without a physician visit, there remains a possibility that the use of these medications may not be fully captured in electronic health records. Another potential limitation is missing vaccination data. Patients with or without COVID-19 vaccination may experience differential outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection, independent of metformin use. Furthermore, the analyzed electronic health records may not include the exact number and date of SARS-CoV-2 infections because of home testing, and the elevated levels of glycated hemoglobin in the metformin group suggest that this group may have included patients with undiagnosed diabetes or prediabetes. There may be several other factors that might have influenced the observed outcomes, such as vague symptoms, access to healthcare, and pre-existing health conditions. However, these are challenges inherent in identifying and diagnosing long COVID. Future clinical trials and further research are needed to clarify the potential benefits of metformin for preventing long COVID and help inform treatment guidelines

Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, and Ruian Ke. The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified during the COVID-19 pandemic by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key operational challenge in viral surveillance is wading through an extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, the authors formulated a novel methodology that represents the distances between small subsets of viral sequences as graph Laplacians. By leveraging these mathematical representations, the team was able to identify specific structural features directly tied to rapid population growth. From early SARS-CoV-2 sequence data collected in the United States and the United Kingdom between 2021 and mid-2022, the investigators identified two primary features—genetic diversity and graph connectivity—that allow the model to reliably estimate the growth rates of newly emerged lineages. Discover more machine learning Learn AI Tools Machine Learning Get Rapid Tests Find Lung Care To test the validity and generalizability of their model, the researchers applied it to viral genomic data collected from mid-2022 to the end of 2024. For data collected in 2023, when sequencing efforts were relatively high with thousands of sequences generated per day in both the United States and the United Kingdom, the model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. Overall, the researchers concluded that their work provides a scalable and adaptable tool to estimate the growth rate of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2 lineages. content_title: Could a common diabetes drug help prevent long COVID?
content: A nationwide study suggests that prescribing the widely used diabetes drug metformin soon after COVID-19 infection may substantially reduce the risk of long COVID or death, reinforcing earlier clinical trial findings. Study: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Image credit: TBamphoto/Shutterstock.com Prescription of metformin within six days of documented severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection is associated with a 53% lower risk of developing long COVID or death over six months, according to a new study published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Metformin emerges as a potential long COVID preventive SARS-CoV-2, the causative pathogen of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, continues to cause new infections across countries. Long COVID refers to symptoms that persist or develop following SARS-CoV-2 infection, typically lasting at least three months, and has become a major public health concern worldwide. Long COVID is also associated with a significant economic burden, highlighting the need for identifying medications that can reduce the risk of developing long COVID. Metformin, a widely used medication for type 2 diabetes, has shown the ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 in in vitro studies. In a randomized clinical trial, patients receiving metformin were found to have lower nasal viral load and a reduced risk of developing long COVID. However, the trial restricted enrollment by age and body mass index, and only 22% were enrolled during the Omicron era. These factors might have restricted the generalizability of its findings to patients with diverse sociodemographic and health conditions. The current study aimed to investigate the association between newly prescribed metformin at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of developing long COVID in a broader sample, using electronic health records. Nationwide health records help assess metformin and long COVID The study analyzed electronic health record data from a nationwide database containing over 21 million individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection from every state in the United States to identify new metformin users who were prescribed the drug within six days of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. New metformin users were compared with those prescribed comparator medications, including fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast, for the risk of long COVID or death within 180 days of the metformin or comparator medication prescription. The researchers excluded patients with documented indications for chronic metformin use, including diabetes and prediabetes, as well as those prescribed metformin or comparator medications in the preceding 12 months. Eligible patients were also required to have attended outpatient visits during both the 0–6-month and 6–12-month periods before infection. Early metformin prescriptions linked to lower long COVID risk The study included 248 patients in the metformin group and a comparator group with a weighted size equivalent to approximately 248 patients. In most cases, medications were prescribed within two days of SARS-CoV-2 infection, suggesting successful identification of patients who were seeking metformin or control medications for their infection. The analysis of primary outcomes showed that, after weighting, about 4% of patients in the metformin group and 8.5% of patients in the control group had long COVID or died, representing an absolute difference of approximately 4.5 percentage points. The adjusted risk ratio analysis indicated that patients who received a metformin prescription within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection had a 53% lower risk of long COVID or death over a 6-month period, compared with those who received a prescription for comparator medications. Further analysis suggested that having a metformin prescription within one day of infection was associated with a 61% lower risk of long COVID or death, whereas having the same prescription within 14 days of infection was associated with a 25% lower risk. Real-world findings reinforce earlier metformin clinical trial results The study provides further evidence of an association between newly prescribed metformin during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and a lower risk of long COVID or death over a period of six months. The association appeared stronger in patients who received metformin earlier in infection. These findings are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that early initiation of antiviral treatment against SARS-CoV-2 infection is more effective in reducing viral replication than late-stage treatment. Previous in vitro studies have also indicated that metformin reduces SARS-CoV-2 RNA while increasing cell viability. Similarly, previous randomized clinical trials have shown reduced viral load in patients using metformin. In the subgroup excluding those with a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription, the study found a slightly higher risk ratio. This finding raises the hypothesis that patients receiving a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription in addition to a new metformin prescription may have a lower risk ratio than the entire study population. Because of the observational design, the study analyses may be limited by missing data and misclassification of exposures, outcomes, and confounders. Since nirmatrelvir–ritonavir could be obtained directly from pharmacies without a physician visit, there remains a possibility that the use of these medications may not be fully captured in electronic health records. Another potential limitation is missing vaccination data. Patients with or without COVID-19 vaccination may experience differential outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection, independent of metformin use. Furthermore, the analyzed electronic health records may not include the exact number and date of SARS-CoV-2 infections because of home testing, and the elevated levels of glycated hemoglobin in the metformin group suggest that this group may have included patients with undiagnosed diabetes or prediabetes. There may be several other factors that might have influenced the observed outcomes, such as vague symptoms, access to healthcare, and pre-existing health conditions. However, these are challenges inherent in identifying and diagnosing long COVID. Future clinical trials and further research are needed to clarify the potential benefits of metformin for preventing long COVID and help inform treatment guidelines. - Bramante CT. (2026). Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Journal of Medical Virology. content: 今日动态 返回首页 会员注册 登录 生物通快讯免费订阅 首页 今日动态 人才市场 新技术专栏 中国科学人 云展台 BioHot 定制我的BioHot 进入我的BioHot 进入我的集采 肿瘤癌症研究 免疫/基因/细胞疗法 神经生物学 健康与疾病 衰老机制与长寿 单细胞技术 基因编辑-CRISPR RNA研究 肠道菌与人体微生态 细胞代谢 AI生物信息学 COVID 云讲堂直播 会展中心 特价专栏 技术快讯 免费试用 生物通官微 陪你抓住生命科技 跳动的脉搏 生物通首页 > 今日动态 > 正文 SARS-CoV-2蛋白质组结构生物学:实验背景、功能解释与干预研究的多维证据框架 《International Journal of Molecular Sciences》:Structural Biology of the SARS-CoV-2 Proteome: Experimental Context, Functional Interpretation, and Intervention Research 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月12日 来源:International Journal of Molecular Sciences 5.6 编辑推荐: 结构生物学已明确了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)蛋白质组的关键特征,但结构覆盖(structural coverage)与功能支持(functional support)仍不均衡。本综述将结构蛋白(structural proteins) 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Review Open access 结构生物学已明确了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)蛋白质组的关键特征,但结构覆盖(structural coverage)与功能支持(functional support)仍不均衡。本综述将结构蛋白(structural proteins)、非结构蛋白(nonstructural proteins)和附属蛋白(accessory proteins)的代表性结构,与来自生化(biochemical)、细胞(cellular)、计算(computational)及干预(intervention)研究的证据相关联。研究人员探讨结构观察(structural observations)何时能够支持生物学解释(biological interpretations),以及何种额外证据可将这些解释与干预结局(intervention outcomes)相连接。在选定的蛋白质(proteins)、复合物(complexes)、病毒粒子(virions)、复制细胞器(replication organelles)及变异株研究(variant studies)中,结构覆盖、实验背景(experimental context)和功能支持被记录为独立的维度(dimensions)。选定案例显示,已解析的结构(resolved structures)可与有争议的功能(disputed functions)共存;在本综述所比较的证据允许的范围内,研究人员指出哪些解释被视为得到充分支持(adequately supported),哪些仍属于候选性解释(candidate explanations)。研究之间的差异也可反映不同尺度上的互补性观察(complementary observations)。抗病毒(antiviral)、抗体(antibody)和疫苗(vaccine)研究展示了结构如何促进设计(design)及其机制学解释(mechanistic interpretation),而临床结局(clinical outcomes)则涉及特定产品(products)、人群(populations)和终点(endpoints)。主要空白(major gaps)涉及天然组装体(native assemblies)、某些附属蛋白发现的生理相关性(physiological relevance),以及分子识别(molecular recognition)向抗病毒效力(antiviral efficacy)或保护性免疫力(protective immunity)的转化。 1. Introduction 结构生物学为严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)病毒功能和干预研究提供了分子参考点。该病毒编码四种结构蛋白——刺突(S)、膜(M)、包膜(E)和核衣壳(N)——以及十六个非结构蛋白(nsps 1–16)和多种附属蛋白。本综述探讨结构观察何时能够支持生物学解释,以及何种额外证据可将其与干预结局相连接。比较沿三个独立维度展开:结构覆盖、实验背景和功能支持。评估标准包括:功能是否在表达该蛋白的内源系统中测量、结构-功能关联是否通过突变得以验证、观察是否在独立系统或独立小组中重现、以及感染期间是否产生该蛋白。 2. Structural Proteins 2.1. Spike (S) Glycoprotein S糖蛋白是同源三聚体I类融合蛋白,也是主要抗原靶点。预融合S胞外域结构采用2P稳定设计,显示一个受体结合域(RBD)向上构象。每个S原聚体含22个潜在N-连接糖基化位点。RBD与血管紧张素转化酶2(ACE2)结合的晶体结构定义了受体结合界面,分子动力学(MD)模拟显示SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2复合物动态降低且静电吸引力增强。跨膜蛋白酶丝氨酸2(TMPRSS2)和内体组织蛋白酶参与蛋白切割。跨膜结构域(TMD)通过核磁共振(NMR)和冷冻电镜解析,显示平行三聚体组装,胞质侧半胱氨酸被棕榈酰化。冷冻电子断层扫描(cryo-ET)显示完整病毒颗粒上S蛋白的铰链样运动和构象多样性,内部核糖核蛋白(RNP)组装呈堆叠排列。RBD内的脂肪酸结合位点可稳定锁定构象。可溶性胞外域不报告膜锚施加的约束。 2.2. Membrane (M) Protein M蛋白是病毒包膜中最丰富的蛋白,含222个氨基酸和三个跨膜螺旋。两种构象的M二聚体已解析,脂质纳米盘中的结构描述了确定膜环境中的二聚体。M与JNJ-9676结合的冷冻电镜结构支持其作为潜在抗病毒靶点。直接脂质相互作用与M构象行为相关。 2.3. Envelope (E) Protein E蛋白是75个氨基酸的小膜蛋白,体外电生理记录显示离子通道活性。固态核磁共振(NMR)解析了其跨膜结构域的五聚体螺旋束。C末端区域与宿主蛋白识别相关,E C末端肽与PALS1片段结合的冷冻电镜结构定义了特异性宿主结合界面。 2.4. Nucleocapsid (N) Protein N蛋白含N端结构域(NTD,参与RNA结合)和C端结构域(CTD,介导二聚化和RNA结合),由内在无序区域连接。NTD晶体结构、NTD-RNA复合物模型及CTD二聚体结构已解析。体外N-RNA混合物可形成凝聚体。cryo-ET揭示了病毒颗粒内RNP组装的空间组织。 3. Nonstructural Proteins and Replication Machinery 3.1. Overview of Nonstructural Proteins and the Replication–Transcription Complex (RTC) 复制转录复合体(RTC)与双膜囊泡(DMV)相关。核心聚合酶复合物由nsp12(RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶,RdRp)、nsp7和nsp8组成。其他酶包括nsp13解旋酶、nsp14(具有3'-5'外切核糖核酸酶(ExoN)和N7-甲基转移酶活性)、nsp15内切核糖核酸酶和nsp16 2'-O-甲基转移酶。扩展RTC结构显示核心聚合酶与nsp9、nsp13、nsp10和nsp14等关联,但不同研究解析的组件不同。nsp3、nsp4和nsp6参与内质网(ER)膜重塑。nsp11是13个氨基酸的肽。 3.2. Nsp1 Nsp1参与调节宿主蛋白合成。分离Nsp1 N端结构域的晶体结构提供了其折叠核心。冷冻电镜和功能分析表征了核糖体相关Nsp1,并将其与细胞蛋白合成抑制关联。 3.3. Nsp2 交联质谱为nsp2架构提供了整合模型。全长模型结合冷冻电镜数据和计算预测,但实验支持因区域而异。保守锌结合基序提示可能的核酸相互作用。 3.4. Main Protease (Mpro/Nsp5) Mpro(又称3C样蛋白酶(3CLpro)或nsp5)是半胱氨酸蛋白酶,在pp1ab的11个典型位点切割复制酶多聚蛋白。成熟酶作为同源二聚体,每个原聚体含两个β桶结构域和C端α螺旋结构域,催化位点含半胱氨酸-组氨酸二元组。早期N3结合结构为基础抑制剂发现提供基础。Mpro与萘瑞特韦(nirmatrelvir)的复合物显示其与催化半胱氨酸(Cys145)形成共价加合物。 3.5. Papain-Like Protease (PLpro/Nsp3 Domain) PLpro参与多聚蛋白加工,并去除宿主蛋白的泛素和干扰素刺激基因15(ISG15)修饰。PLpro含N端泛素样(Ubl)结构域和蛋白酶区(拇指、手掌和手指亚结构域)。PLpro与ISG15 C末端探针共价结合的结构已解析。GRL0617结合结构显示非共ovalent抑制剂占据靠近但独立催化半胱氨酸(Cys111)的位点。 3.6. RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase (RdRp/Nsp12) RdRp(nsp12)与辅助因子nsp7和nsp8一起发挥作用。其聚合酶结构域采用经典右手折叠,含手指、手掌和拇指亚结构域,N端NiRAN域通过界面域连接。RNA-free和RNA-bound聚合酶结构已解析。NiRAN域和nsp9参与非经典RNA加帽途径。瑞德西韦(remdesivir)阻断RNA转位的结构和生化分析支持延迟抑制RNA延伸。 3.7. Helicase (Nsp13) Nsp13是核苷三磷酸依赖的解旋酶,含N端锌结合域和两个具有重组酶A(RecA)样折叠的结构域。代表性晶体结构已解析。片段筛选识别了与早期抑制剂研究相关的结合片段。 3.8. Exoribonuclease (Nsp14 ExoN) and Mismatch Recognition Nsp14是双功能蛋白,含N端ExoN域和C端N7-甲基转移酶域。Nsp10刺激ExoN活性,结构比较将其结合与nsp14盖亚结构域重折叠关联。nsp10-nsp14 ExoN域复合物及RNA-bound冷冻电镜结构为携带3'-末端错配的RNA底物的识别提供分子基础。 3.9. Endoribonuclease (Nsp15 NendoU) Nsp15是类尼多病毒尿苷酸特异性内切核糖核酸酶(NendoU),形成六聚体。在感染期间,该活性拮抗双链RNA(dsRNA)诱导的抗病毒信号。 3.10. 2′-O-Methyltransferase (Nsp16 with Nsp10) Nsp16是298个氨基酸的2'-O-甲基转移酶,与nsp10合作在病毒mRNA加帽中发挥作用。nsp16-nsp10复合物与S-腺苷甲硫氨酸(SAM)和帽相关配体的晶体结构已解析。异四聚体组装包含两个nsp16-nsp10异二聚体。 4. Accessory Proteins 4.1. ORF3a Protein ORF3a是275个氨基酸的膜蛋白。脂质纳米盘中的冷冻电镜结构显示二聚体构象,每个原聚体有三个跨膜螺旋。关于ORF3a是否导电存在争议:一项研究记录通道样活性,另一项研究未发现可归因于ORF3a的可重复电流。ORF3a还阻断HOPS复合物介导的自噬体-溶酶体融合。研究人员不将通道活性视为这些细胞表型的默认解释。 4.2. ORF3c Protein ORF3c由与ORF3a重叠的替代阅读框编码。比较基因组分析支持其蛋白质编码状态,且已证实感染期间的表达。其通过靶向线粒体抗病毒信号蛋白(MAVS)抑制先天感知。 4.3. ORF6 Protein ORF6通过与RNA输出1(Rae1)和核孔蛋白98(Nup98)相互作用破坏核质运输,阻断信号转导子和转录激活子(STAT)蛋白的核输入。NMR研究在重构膜环境中表征了其构象并鉴定了N端膜锚。ORF6 C末端肽与Rae1/Nup98片段结合的晶体结构定义了宿主蛋白结合界面。 4.4. ORF7a and ORF7b Proteins ORF7a具有免疫球蛋白样胞外域,其晶体结构已确定。重组胞外域影响HLA-DR/DP/DQ表面表达。ORF7b是小疏水膜蛋白,固态NMR显示在重构膜环境中主要形成α螺旋构象。 4.5. ORF8 Protein ORF8具有免疫球蛋白样折叠,晶体结构显示同源二聚体。功能研究对IL-17受体参与结论不一。研究人员将ORF8相关炎症反应视为在某些实验系统中得到支持。 4.6. ORF9b and the Putative ORF9c Product ORF9b由N基因内的替代阅读框编码。分离的同源二聚体及与TOM70结合的晶体结构已解析。ORF9c是推定的编码区,但感染期间的蛋白质表达尚未确立。 4.7. ORF10 and ORF3b ORF10是推定的短编码区。ORF10-Cullin-2-ZYG11B复合物在细胞培养条件下不是感染所需的。ORF3b是推定的重叠编码区,比较基因组分析不支持其作为保守蛋白质编码基因。 5. Cross-Protein Assemblies and In Situ Structural Insights cryo-ET揭示了病毒颗粒内S蛋白的构象变化和内部RNP组装。nsp3-nsp4跨膜孔复合体在DMV双膜界面处的结构已被解析。超分辨率成像区分了DMV相关dsRNA和dsRNA颗粒,支持蛋白酶依赖性成熟模型。 6. Effects of Variants on Structure and Function 早期变异株的S蛋白结构显示相似的总体架构但RBD构象群体不同。Omicron研究结合S结构和RBD-抗体复合结构,显示尽管架构广泛保留,但中和活性降低。后续Omicron谱系引入了多个替代,其中一些位于1类抗体表位内。Mpro变异评估显示对特定抑制剂的敏感性取决于化合物和蛋白变体。 7. Structure-Guided Intervention Research: Antivirals, Antibodies, and Vaccines 7.1. Small-Molecule Antivirals 瑞德西韦(remdesivir)的冷冻电镜结构显示其活性形式在聚合酶催化位点,RNA合成在额外核苷酸掺入后停滞。萘瑞特韦(nirmatrelvir)与Mpro的复合物显示其与催化半胱氨酸形成可逆共价键。恩司特韦(ensitrelvir)是非共价Mpro抑制剂。计算筛选提出Mpro抑制剂候选物。 7.2. Therapeutic Antibodies Barnes等的四类方案根据RBD抗体与ACE2位点的关系及其在不同S蛋白构象中的可及性对其进行分组。组合抗体如REGN-COV2和AZD7442结合非重叠表位。完整IgG抗体在病毒颗粒上的cryo-ET显示双价结合。美国FDA撤销了REGEN-COV、sotrovimab、Evusheld和bebtelovimab的紧急使用授权。 7.3. Vaccine Design and Structural Insights 预融合稳定方法 informed SARS-CoV-2抗原设计。HexaPro扩展了2P设计。人研究显示疫苗受者比康复个体具有更高的RBD结合IgG效价,但中和效价与RBD结合IgG效价的比例更低。变异株适应疫苗研究提供了针对更新抗原的血清中和活性。 8. Methodological Challenges and Advances 8.1. Experimental Methods and Sample Context 单颗粒冷冻电镜解析了早期预融合S和聚合酶复合物。缓冲成分(如CHAPS或DDM)可将重构的S蛋白群体移向关闭状态。cryo-ET存在缺失楔问题。X射线晶体学和NMR提供互补信息。蛋白质组的结构覆盖不均一。 8.2. Computational Simulations and Integrative Modeling MD模拟探索构象动力学。结合自由能估计提供了模型依赖描述。虚拟筛选可提名候选物,但需要独立实验评估。AlphaFold预测扩展了结构范围,但预测完整性不意味着均匀实验支持。 9. Outlook 本综述支持特定的分子特征,但从结构到生物功能和临床益处的某些联系仍未解决。主要未解决问题涉及天然组装体中分子组件的组织和功能关系。理解动态需要将结构状态与随时间过程的测量更紧密地联系。S蛋白的跨膜锚定部分是一个特定差距。 10. content: Skip to main content FactCheck.org® A Project of The Annenberg Public Policy Center FactCheck.org® Home Articles FactCheck Posts SciCheck En Español Players Guide 2026 Project 2025 series Debunking Viral Claims Ask a Question Ask FactCheck Ask SciCheck Donate Topics 2026 election President Trump immigration inflation crime healthcare vaccination View All About Us Our Mission Our Process Our Funding Our Staff Undergraduate Fellows Awards Request a Correction Contact Us Search More Newsletter Viral Claims Instagram Threads YouTube TikTok Facebook X FactCheck On the Air FactCheck Posts › SciCheck Florida’s Surgeon General Spins State COVID-19 Vaccine Comparison Study By Jessica McDonald Posted on November 12, 2026 A new analysis of data from Florida found a higher risk of mortality in those receiving the Pfizer versus the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine in the year after a first dose. It does not establish that the Pfizer vaccine was dangerous or caused deaths, contrary to suggestions by the state’s surgeon general or statements by online purveyors of vaccine misinformation. The study did not compare outcomes to unvaccinated people, so it cannot say whether vaccination with either shot was associated with higher or lower mortality overall. The paper acknowledged that one possible reason for Pfizer’s higher relative mortality risk is that the Moderna vaccine was more effective against COVID-19 than the Pfizer shot. The study was published on Nov. 4 in the journal Global Epidemiology and was mostly conducted by members of the Florida Department of Health using state data. It found that compared with a Moderna dose, adult Pfizer recipients had a 40% higher risk of dying from any cause within one year of a first dose. Relative to Moderna, the Pfizer vaccine was also associated with a 91% higher risk of dying from COVID-19, a 57% higher risk of dying from cardiovascular disease and a 37% higher risk of dying from something other than COVID-19, as recorded on a death certificate. Previous research has not found that either vaccine increases mortality. Both vaccines have saved many lives by preventing COVID-19 deaths. Experts told us the study itself, which was upfront about its limitations, is not especially problematic. But some interpretations of it — including by some of the paper’s own authors — are. “As I said in January 2024, no one should be taking mRNA COVID-19 vaccines because of their terrible safety profile,” Dr. Joseph Ladapo, a co-author and Florida’s surgeon general, wrote on X the day after publication. “But for those who had to take one, Florida’s public health data strongly implies that thousands of Floridians died as a result of receiving Pfizer instead of Moderna. The number of lives lost in the U.S. and internationally is staggering, based on this analysis.” Jeffrey S. Morris, the director of biostatistics at the University of Pennsylvania who wrote a detailed critique on X of what the paper can and cannot say, told us that Ladapo’s comment goes beyond the evidence. “That is like orders of magnitude beyond what his own paper showed,” he said. Ladapo, who has a history of promoting flawed studies that argue the mRNA vaccines are dangerous, including one from the Florida Department of Health that claimed to identify a higher risk of cardiac death after vaccination in young men, cited unsubstantiated concerns when calling for a halt in the use of all mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in January 2024. That fall, the Florida Department of Health began advising all people — even older people at high risk of severe COVID-19 — to not get vaccinated with an mRNA vaccine. At the time, and still today, there is only one non-mRNA COVID-19 vaccine available in the U.S., the protein-based Novavax vaccine. No other state recommends against mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. Speaking to Children’s Health Defense, the nonprofit opposed to vaccines that Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. previously led, Ladapo framed the results as indicative of a safety concern, saying the new study helps show that “our system for evaluating vaccine safety is broken.” “The findings of this study should not be interpreted as establishing the overall safety of the Moderna vaccine,” he said, citing prior research that he claimed also raised safety concerns about the Moderna vaccine (we’ve written about that study, too). “We reiterate our recommendation that, based on what is currently known about the safety of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, no one should receive them,” he added. The Florida Department of Health did not respond to our inquiries asking about his interpretation of the study and whether the department shared his views. Online, others made even more explicit claims about the new paper. “This is an extremely important paper. It shows that the Pfizer vaccine was not safe. It killed people. There is no other way to interpret this data,” Steve Kirsch, a former tech entrepreneur who has long spread inaccurate information about the vaccines, said on X on Nov. 5. “An official government study just confirmed that COVID shots resulted in a CATASTROPHIC loss of life,” Nicolas Hulscher, another prominent spreader of vaccine misinformation, wrote on X, sharing a video in which he further claimed that extrapolating the Florida findings to the U.S. would mean “you get a minimum of 330,000 American deaths from Pfizer alone.” These claims are false. Natalie Dean, an associate professor of biostatistics and bioinformatics at Emory University, told us the study isn’t evidence that either of the vaccines is killing people. “I don’t see how this is an indictment of the safety of these vaccines since it’s just a comparison of two different vaccines,” she said. “The way the paper is getting talked about does not align with the actual evidence in the paper,” Morris, who is also a distinguished research fellow with our parent organization, the Annenberg Public Policy Center, said. “The study legitimately demonstrates an association between vaccine brand and subsequent mortality in a selected matched Florida cohort,” he said in an X post. “It does not establish that these differences are causal, much less that they reflect vaccine-related harm.” When asked for comment, a Pfizer spokesperson told us that medical experts and regulatory authorities around the globe have reviewed and approved or recommended the vaccine, and that it continues to be monitored for safety. “With billions of doses of the vaccine administered around the world, the safety profile for the vaccine for all authorized groups continues to be favorable,” the spokesperson said. Study Limitations In the Global Epidemiology paper, the authors attempted to identify similar individuals in the state who received a Pfizer versus a Moderna vaccine in the first eight months of the vaccine rollout. They then looked at death outcomes within a year of the first vaccine dose to estimate relative mortality risk. To try to control for factors other than vaccine brand, the authors matched about 1 million individuals who received a Pfizer vaccine with 1 million who received a Moderna dose on seven different variables. These were age group; sex; race; ethnicity; calendar month of vaccination; type of vaccination site, such as private pharmacy or hospital; and census tract. The authors also did other checks to try to show that this matching was largely successful, finding no statistical difference, for example, when the same pairings were assessed for cancer deaths or suicide or homicide. The problem is that since this is an observational study, there is still concern that the mortality differences observed between the vaccines were not due to the vaccines themselves, but to other factors. Photo by guteksk7 / stock.adobe.com. A key issue Morris and Dean raised is that the vaccine recipients were not matched for medical frailty or underlying health status. If the Pfizer recipients were in poorer overall health or had more risk factors for COVID-19 or other diseases, that could explain a large part of why the Moderna recipients appear to have lower mortality, rather than suggesting anything about the vaccine itself. Then, even if the mortality difference is due to the vaccines, Morris explained in an article on X, it does not necessarily mean that the Pfizer vaccine is causing harm. It may simply be that the Moderna vaccine is better at preventing harm, making the Pfizer vaccine look bad in comparison. “You can see the better effectiveness of the Moderna vaccine in there,” Dean said of the study’s findings. Several studies have found that the Moderna vaccine was slightly more effective at preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes than Pfizer’s. Although quite similar, the original Moderna vaccine contained significantly more mRNA per dose than the Pfizer shot and the second dose was given an extra week apart. Higher protection against COVID-19 could also spill over into the other mortality categories as well, particularly during Florida’s delta variant wave in 2021, Morris said. “Any deaths that were in fact due to COVID, but they didn’t formally get tested would not have been documented as COVID, so they would be in the non-COVID deaths,” he told us. Studies have found that severe COVID-19 infections raise the risk of cardiovascular events and death well after the infection. In the paper, the authors were careful to note many of these caveats, and to say that the findings could be explained by a more protective Moderna vaccine, other factors the researchers were not able to control for, or what they term “non-specific effects” of the vaccines (or some combination thereof). It is nevertheless clear that in public, some of the authors preferred to promote the latter idea, which could include the notion that the Pfizer vaccine has some kind of harmful effect. In a post on X, Retsef Levi, the corresponding author, wrote, “This study adds to a growing evidence that the mRNA COVID vaccines of Moderna and Pfizer may have different non-specific effects.” Levi is a professor at Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s business school who has long said that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines should not be used. He was one of Kennedy’s appointees to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s vaccine advisory committee in June 2025 before a judge paused the appointments and temporarily blocked the group’s decisions in March. In his X post, Levi also pointed to a recent nanoscience study that he said “showed significant differences in systemic persistence of nano-lipids and spike mRNA between Moderna and Pfizer mRNA COVID vaccines!” The senior author of the nanoscience paper, immunologist Stephen Kent of the University of Melbourne, told us in an email that it is “inappropriate to refer to our paper supporting death from Pfizer” and that “it would not be scientifically appropriate to use our findings to draw conclusions about vaccine safety or mortality risks.” He, too, said the observed outcome in the Florida analysis could be related to Moderna protecting against COVID-19 better than Pfizer. Putting the Study in Fuller Context Another argument against jumping to the conclusion that the Pfizer vaccine is actively harming people through an unspecified mechanism is the larger body of research conducted on the COVID-19 vaccines. In particular, there is a Veterans Affairs study published in December 2021 in the New England Journal of Medicine that also compared the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines to one another using a matching approach similar to the one in the Florida analysis. (This study also did not match for health status or comorbidities, but unlike the Florida analysis, it did provide a table showing that the matched pairs did not substantially differ on those parameters.) The study was smaller and over a shorter time period, but it found that the Moderna vaccine recipients had a lower risk of a variety of adverse COVID-19 outcomes. Although not statistically significant, Pfizer recipients were 11% more likely to die from COVID-19 than Moderna recipients. The study did not, however, find any other mortality differences between the vaccines. As a check on their main findings, the authors looked at non-COVID-19 deaths, finding virtually identical patterns of death in matched recipients of both vaccines (see figure S3). “They found absolutely no difference in non-COVID deaths, like not even a trend,” Morris said. A few other studies have identified a slightly higher all-cause mortality after vaccination with various Pfizer shots compared with Moderna, but nothing approaching 40% — and some results have favored the Pfizer vaccine instead. If the Florida study results “were really true and really driven by vaccine harm, we would expect them to be replicated elsewhere, but it doesn’t seem to be,” Morris said. Notably, the studies that have looked at all-cause mortality among vaccinated and unvaccinated people have consistently found much lower rates of death in vaccinated people. A 2025 French study, for example, compared mortality over four years, finding about a 25% lower risk of death in vaccinated versus unvaccinated individuals (with a lower risk for Pfizer than Moderna). Scientists don’t think the vaccines actually lowered death risk by that much because of something called the healthy vaccinee effect. People who choose to get vaccinated are generally healthier than those who don’t — especially closer to the vaccination date, since people near the end of their lives aren’t getting vaccinated. While studies try to adjust for this issue, and longer-running ones are less affected by it, it remains a concern when interpreting the results. Still, these findings do not support the notion that the vaccines are increasing the risk of death. The authors of the French study concluded that “a causal link between mRNA vaccination and excess long-term mortality appears highly unlikely.” For both vaccines to have some kind of toxic effect, as some claim — and for the Pfizer vaccine to have a nearly 40% higher risk of death than Moderna, but not be detected in these sorts of studies — the healthy vaccinee effect would have to be “really enormous,” Morris said. Dean noted that even if the Moderna vaccine is better at protecting against COVID-19, it was still important to have both vaccines as options. When the shots were first rolled out, not only was it not yet known how the two vaccines compare, but there weren’t enough shots of any single brand for all Americans. Some data suggest the Moderna vaccine caused more intense expected side effects, such as a fever, than the Pfizer shot. “For some people, Pfizer has been a better option” because of the milder side effects, she said. “I just don’t understand indicting things backwards.” It’s worth noting that the original versions of the Florida analysis, which were posted to preprint servers, made more sweeping statements more akin to how some authors have presented the paper online, with one preprint concluding that the results are “suggestive of differential non-specific effects” of the two vaccines “and potential concerning adverse effects on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.” The published version lacks these statements. Individuals can now point to a published document “that is going to be hard for people to understand because it’s very complex and there’s a lot of tables,” Dean said, and it can be used to “make more extreme claims.” Editor’s note: FactCheck.org does not accept advertising. title: Severe COVID-19 Hospitalization Multiplies Post-Acute Asthma Flare Risks Without Lasting Control Loss
excerpt: A systematic review reveals that severe COVID-19 hospitalization elevates post-acute asthma exacerbation risks up to fivefold, while long-term asthma control remains largely stable.
